宏福苑火災引起各界對維修工程圍標問題的關注。競委會今年1月曾搜查14間工程承辦商和顧問公司，涉及在全港17個維修工程從事圍標等行為，估計合約總值約七億港元。行動中取得的證據揭發存在另一個圍標集團，競委會今日再搜查4間承辦商、涉及28個大廈維修工程、總值約五億元，涉嫌在投標期間提交「掩護式」標書等。

The Competition Commission announced that yesterday (the 12th), it launched a second round of enforcement action in a bid-rigging case involving building repairs, searching 12 premises, including the offices of four works contractors and the residences of individuals involved. The projects in question cover repair works for 28 housing estates and buildings, with an initial estimated total contract value of approximately HK$500 million. The repair works are distributed across 12 districts in Hong Kong, Kowloon, and the New Territories; some contracts have not yet been awarded, while others commenced or were completed prior to the investigation.

The Competition Commission stated that this operation is a follow-up to the first round of enforcement action in January this year, during which 14 works contractors and consultancy firms were searched, involving 17 repair projects with a total value of approximately HK$700 million. The Commission pointed out that among the evidence obtained in that operation, a suspicious telephone message conversation was discovered, indicating the possible existence of another hidden bid-rigging syndicate intending to target repair works at a certain housing estate. Based on the content of the conversation, a contractor not previously under investigation is suspected of having, through an intermediary, approached other contractors to submit cover bids during the tendering period for the estate's works, but was told in reply that some of those contractors had already been recruited by others to participate in bid-rigging for the same project.

After analysis, the Competition Commission found that the contractor is suspected of having engaged in anti-competitive conduct across multiple projects, including distributing so-called "homework" — instructions on bidding prices — to other contractors to manipulate tender outcomes. Such conduct is suspected of constituting bid-rigging, market sharing, price-fixing collusion, and the exchange of sensitive information, in violation of the Competition Ordinance. Enforcement action has therefore been taken against the contractor, other contractors involved, and relevant individuals. In addition to searching premises, the parties have also been required to surrender documents and information and to attend hearings to provide relevant materials. It is not appropriate at this stage to publicly disclose the subjects of the investigation or details of the case.
